eyebrow: AI Cloud Infrastructure, GPU Computing & MLOps · Chapter 2
subtitle: Lesson 7 · Provisioning GPU Infrastructure

steps.label: No device plugin
steps.sub: a GPU node looks identical to a 0-GPU node to the scheduler

steps.label: NVIDIA device plugin (DaemonSet)
steps.sub: discovers GPUs, reports nvidia.com/gpu as an extended resource

steps.label: kubectl describe node
steps.sub: confirm nvidia.com/gpu under Capacity and Allocatable

code:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: DaemonSet
metadata:
  name: nvidia-device-plugin-daemonset
  namespace: kube-system
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels: { name: nvidia-device-plugin-ds }
  template:
    metadata:
      labels: { name: nvidia-device-plugin-ds }
    spec:
      tolerations:
        - key: nvidia.com/gpu
          operator: Exists
          effect: NoSchedule
      containers:
        - name: nvidia-device-plugin-ctr
          image: nvcr.io/nvidia/k8s-device-plugin:v0.16.2
caption: One pod per GPU node; assumes the driver and Container Toolkit are already installed.

eyebrow: Requesting a GPU in a pod spec
code:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: pytorch-training-job
spec:
  nodeSelector:
    accelerator: nvidia-a100
  containers:
    - name: trainer
      image: pytorch/pytorch:2.4.0-cuda12.1-cudnn9-runtime
      command: ["python", "train.py"]
      resources:
        limits:
          nvidia.com/gpu: 1
caption: nvidia.com/gpu is limits-only, requests must equal limits, and it's allocated as a whole integer.
